title: The Church as field hospital
hookLine: Francis described the Church as a field hospital for the wounded
tomorrow: Doña Carmen wants to "put her house in order." what does that mean?

lines: HALF DEAD ON THE JERICHO ROAD.
cards: Not the hospital with a gift shop and a parking garage. A field hospital: a tent near the fighting, mud on the floor, the wounded carried in on stretchers.

That's the picture Pope Francis reached for when he described what the Church should be. And Luke tells a story where a field hospital gets set up in the dirt. A man lies half dead on the road down to Jericho.
A priest comes by, sees him, and crosses to the other side. A Levite does the same. Then a Samaritan, not the hero Jesus's listeners would expect, pulls up beside him.

teach.b: What he does first is the whole point. He doesn't ask how the man got there, or whose side he's on, or what he did to deserve it.

teach.h: OIL AND WINE ON THE WOUNDS.
teach.b: In the Douay-Rheims Bible, he "bound up his wounds, pouring in oil and wine." Then he lifts him onto his own animal, brings him to an inn, and pays for his care.
Francis put it plainly in an interview: when someone is badly wounded, you don't ask about his cholesterol or his blood sugar. You heal the wounds first. Everything else can come after.
Something worth repeating tonight: the parable isn't about priests being bad.
It's about who stops, and Jesus gives the role to an outsider. A field hospital doesn't choose its patients.
In a parish, it looks like a meal dropped off, a ride to a treatment, someone bringing communion to the homebound, a hall where a recovery group meets on folding chairs.

how: Catholic parishes carry out the field-hospital work through ministries to the sick and homebound, extraordinary ministers bringing communion, meal trains, Catholic Charities and hospital chaplains.

games.q: what does “the church as field hospital” mean?
o: a chapel set up beside a military camp
a Church that treats wounds before questions
a hospital run by priests and religious sisters

games.q: the field hospital on the road — tap the pairs.
p: what he poured on the wounds
where he paid for the man's care
the Church as a field hospital

s: in the parable, the priest and the Levite stop to help
they pass by on the other side. the Samaritan stops.
the parable's point is that religious people are bad
it's about who stops, and Jesus gives the role to an outsider.
Francis said you treat a badly wounded person's injuries before asking about cholesterol
heal the wounds first; the rest can come after.

games.q: a man comes to the parish food pantry clearly drunk, asking for something to eat. a volunteer wants to lecture him first. what does the field hospital picture say?
o: feed him first; any talk can come later.
send him away until he comes back sober.
hand him a pamphlet on drinking, then food.
games.why: the Samaritan asked nothing before he bound up the wounds. Francis: heal the wounds first, then talk about the rest.

practice: Bring to mind one person who's hurting right now: someone sick, someone grieving, someone home alone. Send them a short message, or decide on one small thing you could bring them.
Then let the sit hold them in mind, the way the Samaritan held the man steady on the road.

wordCard.voice: The Church as field hospital. Pope Francis's picture: a tent near the battle, treating wounds before asking questions.

orig.note: Greek, Luke 10:34: the wounds the Samaritan bound up.

carryVoice: Your line: heal wounds first, the way the Samaritan did before asking a single question. Good night.
